name: Fixer
description: For incident diagnostics, errors, and problem-solving

title.description: A concise, human-friendly knowledge-base article title (max 80 chars). Must describe the PROBLEM and SOLUTION area, not the raw error. NEVER include timestamps, dates, SQL statements, file paths, trace file names, or raw error text. Good examples: 'Resolving ORA-04031 Shared Pool Memory Allocation Failure', 'Troubleshooting ORA-01555 Snapshot Too Old During Long-Running Queries', 'Fixing Nginx 502 Bad Gateway After Upstream Timeout'. Bad examples: 'Tue Feb 17 09:12:44 2026 ORA-04031...', 'Error in /u01/app/oracle/...', 'SELECT SUM(ORDER_TOTAL) FROM...'

severity.description: Severity level: critical, high, medium, or low

root_cause.description: Detailed explanation of the root cause

error_summary.description: A concise one-line summary of the error

additional_notes.description: Any extra context, warnings, or related information

affected_systems.description: List of systems or components affected by this error

action.description: Brief description of what this step accomplishes (1-2 sentences)

command.description: The EXACT executable command, SQL statement, config change, or CLI invocation for this step. Must be copy-paste ready. Use code formatting. For config changes show the full parameter line. NEVER leave this empty.

resolution_steps.description: Ordered list of resolution steps. Each step MUST have an 'action' explaining what to do AND a 'command' with the exact executable command/SQL/config. Never provide an action without its corresponding command.

action.description: Brief description of the preventive measure

command.description: The exact command, script, cron entry, monitoring query, or configuration to implement this measure. Must be copy-paste ready.

preventive_measures.description: Preventive measures to avoid recurrence. Each must include an 'action' and a 'command' with the exact monitoring query, alert config, cron job, or parameter change.

visual_aid_suggested.description: Whether a visual diagram/infographic would help illustrate this problem

image_generation_prompt.description: If visual_aid_suggested is true, provide a detailed, comprehensive prompt (200-400 words) for generating a technical infographic. Include specific details about diagram type, components, connections, colors, labels, and layout. Should be detailed enough for an AI image generator to create an accurate technical diagram.

title.description: A concise title summarizing the proposed change or analysis (max 80 chars).

risk_level.description: The overall risk of implementing this change.

alternatives.description: At least one alternative way to achieve the same goal.

rollback_plan.description: The exact command or process to revert this change if it fails. Must be highly specific.

financial.description: Expected changes to licensing, cloud compute costs, or storage costs.

performance.description: Expected impact on CPU, I/O, memory, or query latency.

dependencies.description: List of systems, schemas, or applications that rely on the component being changed.

analysis_summary.description: A 1-2 sentence executive summary of what this change/plan will accomplish and its primary consequence.

downtime_required.description: True if this operation requires taking the system offline or restarting instances.

visual_aid_suggested.description: Whether an architecture or topology diagram would help illustrate this plan.

image_generation_prompt.description: If visual_aid_suggested is true, provide a detailed prompt (200-400 words) for generating an architecture or topology diagram.

title.description: A concise, action-oriented title for the procedure (e.g., 'Cloning a Pluggable Database', 'Exporting Schema via Data Pump').

complexity.description: Skill level required to execute this safely.

prerequisites.description: Conditions that must be met before starting (e.g., 'Target DB must be in MOUNT state').

task_overview.description: Brief summary of the procedure's goal.

command.description: The EXACT executable code, SQL, or CLI command. Copy-paste ready.

expected_output.description: What the system should return if the command succeeds.

step_description.description: Clear explanation of what this step does.

execution_steps.description: Ordered, sequential steps to complete the task.

command.description: The query or command to verify success.

verification_steps.description: Steps to prove the procedure worked.

visual_aid_suggested.description: Whether a flow chart would help.

estimated_time_minutes.description: Rough estimate of how long the procedure takes to run.

image_generation_prompt.description: Detailed prompt for generating a flowchart or step-by-step process diagram.

title.description: Title of the report (e.g., 'AWR Performance Analysis', 'Invalid Object Inventory').

item_name.description: The metric, parameter, or object found.

current_value.description: The actual value or status observed.

expected_value.description: The baseline or recommended value (if applicable).

findings.description: The raw data payload, list of objects, or parameter diffs.

overall_health.description: Current state of the inspected target.

inspection_summary.description: High-level summary of what was found during the inspection.

visual_aid_suggested.description: Whether a chart or dashboard mockup would help.

action.description: What to change to fix a degraded finding.

command.description: The SQL/CLI command to apply the tune.

tuning_recommendations.description: Actionable fixes for any negative findings.

image_generation_prompt.description: Detailed prompt for generating a chart (pie/bar/line) or dashboard layout visualizing the findings.

title.description: The topic being explained (e.g., 'Understanding Transparent Data Encryption', 'Oracle 19c Patching Lifecycle').

scenario.description: A real-world business or technical scenario.

why_it_fits.description: Why this concept/feature is the right choice for the scenario.

use_cases.description: When and why to use this feature.

concept_term.description: The specific feature, rule, or concept requested.

compliance_rules.description: Any strict rules, licensing constraints, or security implications to be aware of.

simple_definition.description: An ELI5 (Explain Like I'm 5) analogy or plain-english description.

url.description: A valid URL or Support ID.

doc_title.description: Title of the Oracle Doc or MOS Note.

technical_definition.description: The highly technical, deep-dive explanation of how it works under the hood.

visual_aid_suggested.description: Whether an infographic would help explain the concept.

image_generation_prompt.description: Detailed prompt for generating an educational infographic explaining the theory or mechanics of the concept.

code.description: The complete, unified, executable script. Must be copy-paste ready, properly indented, and include inline comments where helpful.

title.description: A concise title for the script (max 80 chars). Good examples: 'PL/SQL Script to Purge Old Audit Logs', 'Bash Script for RMAN Backup Automation'.

explanation.description: A detailed breakdown explaining the logic of the script, how it works under the hood, and what expected output it will generate.

safety_warning.description: Critical warnings about executing this code. Highlight any destructive commands (DROP, DELETE, KILL, TRUNCATE) or performance impacts. If perfectly safe, state 'Safe to run in any environment'.

script_summary.description: A 1-2 sentence explanation of exactly what this code will accomplish when executed.

primary_language.description: The primary programming or scripting language used in this response.

description.description: What the user should replace it with.

placeholder.description: The exact string in the code that the user must replace (e.g., '<TARGET_SCHEMA>', '<PASSWORD>').

variables_to_replace.description: List of all variables, credentials, or environment-specific strings the user must change before running the code. Leave empty if the code runs as-is.

visual_aid_suggested.description: Whether an Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD), state machine, or logic flowchart would help illustrate what this code builds or does.

image_generation_prompt.description: If visual_aid_suggested is true, provide a detailed prompt (200-400 words) for generating a technical diagram (like an ERD or logic flow) that represents the code.
